scope: 14 published source records, including foundational equation proposals and existing sources refreshed at inspected portions; not 14 independent validation trials.

sources.title: Mifflin et al.: a new predictive equation for resting energy expenditure
sources.populationAndWindow: 498 healthy adults, 247 women and 251 men, ages 19–78; 264 normal-weight and 234 obese.
sources.measurement: Indirect calorimetry; original coefficients 9.99W + 6.25H − 4.92A + 166S − 161. Authors also give the rounded form implemented by Metron.
sources.finding: Published arithmetic is supported; derivation fit is not independent validation or an individual accuracy guarantee.
sources.limitations: Healthy derivation population; no transfer to the complete pathological spectrum established.
sources.inspectedPortions: Primary PubMed/publisher indexed abstract and metadata; full methods not inspected.
sources.rightsStatus: Original publisher copyright; broad reuse rights unverified.
sources.republication: Bibliographic pointers and original analysis only. Source text, figures and tables are not relicensed under repository MIT.

sources.title: ten Haaf and Weijs: resting energy expenditure in recreational athletes
sources.populationAndWindow: 90 Dutch recreational athletes, 53 men and 37 women, ages 18–35; 103 initially tested, 13 excluded.
sources.measurement: Vmax Encore n29 hood calorimetry; 30 minutes with first five discarded, CV <10%. Bod Pod composition. Minimum four-hour fast, mean 9.1±4.6 hours; no exercise for 12 hours.
sources.finding: Cunningham within ±10% for 84.9% of men and 78.4% of women; Mifflin below 50%. Table 4 uses 500 + 22FFM and the original unrounded Mifflin coefficients.
sources.limitations: Equation-development results are not independent external validation. Published Mifflin variant differs from Metron rounded form; no reanalysis here. Athlete sampling, preparation and ADP do not transfer to all users.
sources.inspectedPortions: Publisher abstract, methods, results, limitations and licence; published institutional PDF Table 4 checked directly.
sources.rightsStatus: Publisher states Creative Commons Attribution; licence version not independently confirmed.

sources.title: Weijs: prediction validity in US and Dutch overweight and obese adults
sources.populationAndWindow: Adults ages 18–65, BMI 25–40. US abstract says 338 (180 women, 158 men); indexed publisher results/Table 1/Table 4 say 239 (137 women, 102 men). Dutch sample 208 is consistent.
sources.measurement: Indirect calorimetry; Dutch preparation overnight or at least four-hour fast and stable gas exchange. Full US method reconciliation unavailable.
sources.finding: Abstract reports US Mifflin accuracy 79% within ±10%, bias −1%, RMSE 136 kcal/day. Dutch leading equations differ.
sources.limitations: US denominator discrepancy remains unresolved. No authoritative combined US sample count, pooling or sample weighting. Not a direct Mifflin-versus-Cunningham superiority comparison.
sources.inspectedPortions: PubMed abstract and publisher indexed methods/results/Table 1/Table 4. Direct publisher full-page access returned 403.

sources.title: Sordi et al.: predicted versus measured RMR in cross-training participants
sources.populationAndWindow: 65 novice/advanced cross-training participants, 31 men and 34 women; injuries, chronic disease and physical limitations excluded.
sources.measurement: FitMate PRO calorimetry uses fixed RQ 0.85; 15-minute test. InBody 570 estimates composition. Eight-hour fast, no exercise previous day, avoid caffeine 12 hours.
sources.finding: Cunningham is among the most discrepant tested equations. Table 1 labels Cunningham 1991 but specifies 500 + 22FFM, matching Metron arithmetic. Mifflin is not compared.
sources.limitations: Device/preparation and BIA-derived FFM affect comparability. BIA device RMR output is an estimate, not an independent measured reference. Cannot infer Mifflin superiority.
sources.inspectedPortions: Primary PMC full text: abstract, methods, Table 1, results, exclusions and licence.
sources.republication: Bibliographic pointers and original analysis only. Source text, figures and tables are not relicensed under repository MIT.

sources.title: Siedler et al.: performance of 15 bioimpedance devices
sources.populationAndWindow: 73 healthy adults ages 19–50; 37 returned after 12–16 weeks. Online 21 November 2022.
sources.measurement: 15 BIA devices versus a four-compartment reference incorporating ADP, DXA and bioimpedance spectroscopy.
sources.finding: Device repeatability and agreement with reference are different properties; composition input uncertainty remains material.
sources.limitations: Not a validation of enable SECA mBCA 515 or a universal consumer BIA error distribution. Do not propagate these device errors into an individual Metron interval.

sources.title: Brandl et al.: machine learning predictions of resting metabolic rate
sources.populationAndWindow: enable Freising 351 and Nuremberg 103, same 454-person source family as Metron G3. Authors also evaluate Kiel 361; those participant files are not admitted by Metron. Ahead 6 January, online 29 January 2026.
sources.measurement: COSMED Quark RMR hood calorimetry and SECA mBCA 515 composition, as documented in inspected methods and frozen G3 provenance. Source uses Lasso development, distinct from Metron fixed equations.
sources.finding: Adds publication provenance for the same source cohort; does not supply independent replication of Metron G3.
sources.limitations: Training fit, authors’ held-out evaluation and our fixed-equation paired evaluation answer different questions. No new participant records downloaded.

sources.title: Kfir, Lahav and Gepner: prediction of RMR using fat-free mass
sources.populationAndWindow: 3,001 Israeli nutrition-clinic patients ages 20–95, 52% women; random 2,251 development and 750 validation split.
sources.measurement: DXA; Quark RMR mask, 12-hour fast, no exercise for 24 hours, 20-minute rest, 21-minute recording with first five discarded.
sources.finding: Authors report Mifflin and Cunningham underprediction; formula identity for the reported Cunningham output is unresolved.
sources.limitations: Citation names 1980, but implemented coefficients were not located. Reported Cunningham mean 1,521 and mean FFM 53.3 do not reconcile with 500 + 22 × mean FFM. This flags uncertainty, not proof of a different implementation. Methods and Table 1 also interchange thyroid/bariatric subgroup counts (46/136); no disease-specific conclusions admitted.

sources.title: Cai et al.: RMR equations in healthy community-dwelling Chinese older adults
sources.populationAndWindow: 189 adults ages 60–94 in Shanghai; 132 development and 57 validation. Cancer, diabetes, anemia, thyroid disease and RMR-altering medications/hormones excluded; stable weight required.
sources.measurement: DXA and Quark CPET canopy; 12-hour fast, 15–20-minute rest and 60-minute measurement with reported steady-state criteria.
sources.finding: In the 57-person validation split, Mifflin 49.1% and the new Cai model 82.5% within ±10%. Table 1 labels Cunningham (1980) but uses 501.6 + 21.6FFM.
sources.limitations: Reported 10.5% Cunningham accuracy is not performance of Metron 500 + 22FFM. Internal split is not independent-site replication; authors note weak performance at age ≥80.
sources.inspectedPortions: PMC abstract, methods, Table 1, Table 8, limitations and licence. Publisher direct access returned 429.
sources.republication: Bibliographic pointers and original analysis only. Source text, figures and tables are not relicensed under repository MIT.

sources.title: Dong et al.: RMR prediction in Chinese older adults with sarcopenia
sources.populationAndWindow: 43 free-living adults age ≥60 in Suzhou meeting AWGS 2019 sarcopenia criteria. Online 7 May 2026.
sources.measurement: Indirect calorimetry in abstract; exact device, equation coefficients and accuracy definition not verified from full methods.
sources.finding: All 11 equations have reported accuracy below 40%; Mifflin_W has the lowest reported bias, 16.54%, and RMSE 216.51 kcal/day.
sources.limitations: Relative best performance can still be poor. Do not pool its accuracy with verified ±10% definitions or infer all older/frail patients are equivalent. Severity, treatment and intersecting conditions unresolved.

sources.title: Del Biondo et al.: prediction of REE in midlife females
sources.measurement: Indirect calorimetry and DXA lean soft tissue; exact Cunningham variant and full preparation protocol unverified.
sources.finding: Abstract measured minus predicted mean ± SE: Cunningham −157.8 ±28.7 and Mifflin −18.5 ±31.7 kcal/day.
sources.limitations: A nonsignificant mean difference is not equivalence or individual agreement. Lean soft tissue is not automatically FFM. Perimenopause is not pregnancy/lactation; treatment and clinical intersections not reviewed.

sources.title: Xu et al.: RMR equation validity in Chinese nursing-home residents
sources.populationAndWindow: 156 residents of one 300-bed Chinese nursing home, 59 men/97 women, mean age 83.4; measured November–December 2023. 45.5% at malnutrition risk.
sources.measurement: CCM Express hood VO2/VCO2 calorimetry after eight-hour fast, 15-minute rest and 30-minute steady-state measurement; InBody S10 FFM after 12-hour fast. Table 1 uses exact 500 + 22FFM and rounded Mifflin.
sources.finding: Within ±10%: Cunningham 45.5%, Mifflin 17.3%. Cunningham measured-minus-predicted limits of agreement −419.7 to 473.9 kcal/day despite small mean bias.
sources.limitations: Selected single facility. Excluded pulmonary disease, fever, rheumatoid arthritis, thyroid/metabolic disease, anesthetics/benzodiazepines and enteral feeding; final sample without significant disability. Not the whole institutionalized or frail population.
sources.inspectedPortions: Publisher full text: methods, Table 1, results, individual-agreement limits, exclusions and licence.
sources.republication: Bibliographic pointers and original analysis only. Source text, figures and tables are not relicensed under repository MIT.
